references.text: Jacob sees Esau coming with four hundred men and prepares for the meeting. This is the direct follow-up to Jacob sending messengers to Esau.
Esau settled in the Seir mountains, away from his brother Jacob. This explains why Jacob sends a message to 'Seir, the land of Edom'.
Esau was given the nickname Edom ('the red one'), which explains the term 'land of Edom' used in this verse.
Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and planned to kill him. This is the background for why Jacob sends messengers to reconcile with Esau.
The Lord gave the Seir mountains to Esau as a possession, confirming that Esau was settled in Seir when Jacob sent messengers to him.
Obadiah prophesies judgment against Esau/Edom for violence toward his brother Jacob, reflecting the long-standing conflict between the two brothers.
Explains the geographical and relational background (the separation) that makes Jacob's sending of messengers in 32:4 necessary.
Marks narratively the end of the fear Rebekah expressed earlier, and the transition from flight to reunion.
Creates a theological contrast between Jacob's personal meeting with Esau in Seir and Israel's command to respect Esau's inheritance there.
Highlights how God's plan for Esau (protection) applies both nationally (Deut 2) and personally (Jacob's meeting).
Confirms the geographical and political situation (Esau as lord of Seir) that forms the framework for the sending of messengers.
Creates a theological arc from flight (mentioned in 35:1) to the fearful reunion (in 32:4).
